findings.title: `queued` timestamp is evaluated once at import
findings.body: `queued` is assigned a default of `timezone.now()`, which Python evaluates once when the module is imported. Every `AssignmentSource` created without an explicit `queued` value therefore carries the process start time instead of the time the assignment was queued. The field is serialized into the Celery task payload, so the value is misleading and any freshness/dedup logic based on it would be wrong. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. Relatedly, `from_dict` passes a supplied `queued` value through unchanged, so an ISO string produced by JSON serialization remains a string despite the `datetime` annotation.

findings.title: Cycle guard suppresses outbound sync for all links in the source integration
findings.body: `AssignmentSource` stores only `integration_id`, and `should_sync` returns False whenever the target external issue's integration matches the source. `sync_group_assignee_outbound` iterates every `GroupLink` for the group, so if one Sentry group is linked to multiple external issues in the same Jira/GitHub integration, an inbound assignment on one issue will not propagate to the other linked issues (for example, Jira A unassigns, Sentry unassigns, but Jira B stays assigned). The loop that needs breaking is the echo back to the triggering external issue; carry the external issue key in `AssignmentSource` and compare that, or explicitly document that all links in the source integration are intentionally skipped.

findings.title: New cycle-prevention tests cover only assign with one integration
findings.body: The added matching-source test exercises only `GroupAssignee.objects.assign` and only a single linked external issue. It does not cover the `deassign` path, which was also changed to forward `assignment_source`, nor does it verify the claimed behavior that other linked integrations still receive the outbound update. A regression that skips all outbound sync whenever any source is present, or that fails to propagate the source on deassign, would pass these tests. Add a deassign matching-source test and a two-integration test asserting the non-source integration is still called.
